sections.html:
Stamford is a Fairfield County city on Long Island Sound, 34 miles from New York City, with 135,470 residents at the 2020 census. It is Connecticut's second-largest city after Bridgeport and the largest by area, at 52.09 square miles, of which 14.41 is water. It borders Greenwich to the west, Darien to the east, New Canaan to the northeast and Pound Ridge, New York to the north. A mayor and a Board of Representatives govern the city.

Prices and house styles vary sharply from one part of town to the next, so the first thing a buyer wants to know is where your house sits.

Stamford has about 45 distinct neighborhoods and villages, among them Cove, East Side, Downtown, North Stamford, Glenbrook, West Side, Turn of River, Waterside, Springdale, Belltown, Ridgeway, Newfield, South End, Shippan, Roxbury and Palmers Hill.

North of the Merritt Parkway is North Stamford, the largest section by land and the least densely populated. Cove Island on the southern shoreline is a beach and recreation area. Glenbrook and Springdale have stations on the New Canaan branch rail line, and the South End includes the Harbor Point development.

Name the neighborhood when you describe your house. A buyer picturing a condo near the train station is not looking for the same thing as one who wants an acre north of the Merritt.

Stamford has more renters than owners, and building has been heavy downtown and on the waterfront. Harbor Point is an 80-acre mixed-use project south of downtown. For a single-family seller, the buyer pool includes owner-occupants, small landlords who see the large renter share, and investors. For a two-family or small multifamily property, tenant status is the main thing to sort out before a sale.

Stamford is a corporate city. Charter Communications, Philip Morris International, Synchrony Financial, Indeed, Webster Bank, United Rentals, Gartner, Pitney Bowes and WWE all have headquarters here, and it has the largest financial district in the New York region outside New York City.

Transfers and relocations keep some houses changing hands, and an owner with a start date elsewhere often needs a firm closing day more than the last dollar of price.

Stamford sits on the Sound and gets about 51.6 inches of precipitation a year, with roughly 34 inches of snow. Tropical storms are uncommon, but hurricanes have made landfall on the Connecticut coast in 1903, 1938, 1944, 1954, 1960, 1985 and 2012 (Sandy).

  • For waterfront and low-lying parcels, check flood zone status with your insurance agent.
  • In low areas, inspect the basement for past water entry before a buyer does.
  • Wet snow and rain stress roofs and gutters in winter.

Flood maps and insurance rules change, so rely on your lender or insurer for the current status of your parcel.

Stamford has the second-busiest station on the Metro-North system after Grand Central Terminal. Trains run on the New Haven Line, the average nonstop commute is 47 minutes, and the first Grand Central departure is at 4:43 a.m. Amtrak's Acela and Northeast Regional trains also stop here, Interstate 95 and the Merritt Parkway cross the city, and CT Transit buses leave from a terminal beside the station on State Street.

Walking distance to the station is one of the strongest selling points in the city, so put the distance in what you give a buyer. Houses far from the station depend more on highway access and school boundaries, which are set by Stamford Public Schools.

sections.h2: Conveyance tax at a Stamford closing
sections.html:
The seller pays Connecticut's conveyance tax. On most homes it is one percent of the price: 0.75 percent to the state and 0.25 percent to the city (Section 12-494, Chapter 223). Once a residential price passes $800,000, a higher bracket applies. The state rate is 1.25 percent on the part from $800,000 to $2.5 million, and 2.25 percent on the part above that.

The grantor files Form OP-236 when the deed is recorded, and electronic filing through myCTREC is available in participating towns. Stamford's town code is 135. Ask the Stamford city clerk's office whether the city is on the electronic system and whether any extra municipal rate applies.

Connecticut leaves the schedule to each municipality, which may bill in one, two or four installments. The only outer limit is that the final installment cannot be due later than 45 days before the fiscal year closes (Chapter 204). Ask the Stamford Tax Collector for the installment dates and for a payoff or proration figure before closing, and the Assessor for the current assessment.

A late installment accrues interest at 18 percent a year, with a $2 minimum unless the city waives it.

sections.h2: Is a cash sale a good fit?
sections.html:
It can be, especially for a house that needs work or a seller who cannot wait. A cash offer does not depend on the buyer's mortgage, so it avoids a financing contingency that sometimes collapses late.

Because Stamford prices are high, compare carefully. A listing may net more if you can renovate and wait, while a cash sale gives certainty. We buy Stamford houses as-is and will explain the numbers either way.

Whichever way you go, gather the deed, the latest mortgage statement and tax bill, hire a closing attorney, and bring photo ID and all keys to the table. Payoffs come out of your proceeds.

faqs.a: Fairfield County, on Long Island Sound about 34 miles from New York City.

faqs.q: How many people live in Stamford?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 135,470, making it Connecticut's second most populous city.

faqs.q: How much is the conveyance tax when selling in Stamford?
faqs.a: On most homes it is one percent, with 0.75 percent to the state and 0.25 percent to the city. The state rate rises to 1.25 percent on the part of a residential price above $800,000.

faqs.q: Can a Stamford house in a flood-prone area still sell?
faqs.a: Yes. Buyers and lenders will want the flood zone status and any insurance history, and a cash buyer can often work around those issues.

faqs.q: How long is the train ride from Stamford to Grand Central?
faqs.a: The average nonstop commute on Metro-North is 47 minutes.
